done.why: I got the painting into the trophy case, which was what I came for, and after thirty-odd turns of a maze where every room reads identically and most paths dump me back in the troll room, I ran out of ways to find anything new. The east passage was 'unfinished', the ramp unclimbable, the dead end empty.

about: A white house with a trophy case that wants filling, and an underground beneath it where somebody keeps barring the trap door behind you. You go down, find a painting a vandal with taste would have taken, and have to figure out the chimney loop back up with only the lantern and one thing in your hands. The maze under the troll room is a trap of sameness that mostly spits you back out where you started. It's about getting one beautiful thing home when the way you came is shut.

ending.what: No ending was announced. I put the painting in the trophy case and it said 'Your collection of treasures consists of: A painting', which felt like the goal, but nothing closed the story.

moments.note: 'walk around the house' just worked and moved me to the north side.
'keep going around the house' was not recognized right after 'walk around the house' was.
The trophy case 'has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.'
'go down the stairs' refused with 'You can't do that!' when the staircase was right there; plain 'go down' worked.
Trap door crashed shut and someone barred it. The sword started glowing.
Said hello to the troll and he bowed his head in greeting.
He'd just bowed to me, then 'You can't talk to the troll!'
One swing took his head off and black fog ate the body.
East passage unfinished, note pinned: 'Back soon. -- The Management.'
'look around' in the maze gives no exits, no hints, just the same sentence.
'drop the leaflet here' said I can't see any such thing, though I had it.
'what am I carrying?' and 'what do I have' both not recognized; only the word 'inventory' worked.
Lost in identical rooms, no sense of place.
'look into the chasm' answered 'You can't look inside a chasm.'
The gallery: vandals with exceptional taste, one painting left for me.
The painting description, 'hard to look at it for long, and harder to look away.'
The chimney has room for me, a light, and one thing more. A real choice about what to carry.
Chimney came out in the kitchen; the house loops.
'Your collection of treasures consists of: A painting.'
My leaflet marker was exactly where I'd dropped it, so the trick worked.
South then south again landed me back on my own leaflet.
One-way drop, warning only once I'd already gone through.
'search the walls' answered 'You can't look inside a surrounding wall.'

wished: Ask what I'm carrying in plain words instead of having to guess the word 'inventory'.
Have the maze rooms tell me which ways are open, or differ from each other at all.
Get back up the one-way drop, or be warned before taking it.
Find out who keeps barring the trap door, or see them.
Find a second treasure; the only other exits were an unfinished passage and an unclimbable ramp.
Actually talk to the troll after he bowed to me.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: It told me what to do with treasure without any instruction.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: Suddenly there was someone else in the house and I was sealed in.
Funny, and it made the unfinished passage feel deliberate rather than broken.

lines.line: It is a painting of a sunlit valley, done with such tenderness that it is hard to look at it for long, and harder to look away.
lines.why: Made the treasure feel worth carrying.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, a light to climb by and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: Clear rule, clear choice; the painting had to be the one thing.

lines.line: Your collection of treasures consists of: A painting
lines.why: The moment I knew I'd done what I came to do.

lines.line: You won't be able to get back up to the tunnel you are going through when it gets to the next room.
lines.why: A warning that arrived after the choice was made.

fun.why: The house, the troll, the gallery and the chimney loop were a satisfying arc; the maze then ate the second half of my session with nothing to show for it.

engagement.why: The barred trap door and the chimney rule kept me thinking about how to get the painting home; I was leaning in until the maze flattened everything.

difficulty.why: The main path was fair, with the chimney limit a clean puzzle, but the maze gave no feedback at all and the parser refused natural phrasings like 'go down the stairs' and 'what am I carrying?'.

interestingness.why: A troll that bows, a note from the Management, vandals with taste, someone unseen barring doors: the world kept hinting at a personality behind it.

prose.why: Short, dry, and often lovely: the trophy case, the painting, the scuffed dust on the trap door. The maze text, by design or not, is nothing.
